source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text: Rust / Gray leaf spot (ជម្ងឺច្រះស្លឹក, Rust spot or Gray leaf spot): this disease is caused by the fungus Puccinia sorghi (as recorded in the source). Symptoms include lesions of moderate size that occur along the leaf, with a whitish, rust-like powdery coating due to the fungal spores, which can spread very rapidly. This disease is common and tends to appear during the corn's tasseling stage. It is often first observed as small yellowish spots on the leaves. After the spots appear, they enlarge and darken over time, taking on a rust-brown color and a rough, blistered appearance. When infection is severe, it damages the leaves, causing them to dry up and reducing photosynthesis in the corn crop.
